summary: Korea faces a new normal as record heat and drought become permanent climate features.
Emergency responses are no longer sufficient for addressing extreme weather patterns.
Long-term adaptation strategies must replace temporary crisis management approaches.
editorial.stance: Urgent call for Korea to shift from reactive emergency measures to proactive climate adaptation planning.
summaryTr: 한국은 기록적인 폭염과 가뭄이 영구적인 기후 특성이 되면서 새로운 정상 상태에 직면하고 있다.

editorial.bodyTr: 한국이 새로운 현실에 직면하고 있다. 기록적인 폭염과 장기간의 가뭄은 더 이상 고립된 기상이변이 아니라 우리 시대를 규정하는 특징이 되어가고 있다.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Military Academy Joins Judiciary and Prosecution in 'Triple Retaliation
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung justifies military academy merger as accountability for coup, sparking controversy
Allegations of 'three-pronged retaliation' emerge as judiciary, prosecution, and military face restructuring
Concerns over security gaps and privatization of state affairs spreading
editorial.bodyTr: President Lee Jae-myung's push to integrate military academies, citing the former Army Academy's historical responsibility for coups, has intensified controversy over what is being characterized as a third wave of retaliatory measures following actions against the judiciary and the prosecution. As judicial reform legislation and restrictions on prosecutorial investigative authority have been followed by military system restructuring, concerns are mounting both domestically and internationally about security gaps and the privatization of state governance.

editorial.title: [사설] 형소법 안 읽은 대통령, 해석 제각각 주무장관
editorial.body: 입력 업데이트 종합 26면 2026.08.07 00:16 2026.08.07 00:13 2026.08.06 18:06 이재명 대통령이 주재한 그제 국무회의에서 국민이 귀를 의심할 수밖에 없는 발언이 속출했다. 이 대통령은 “개정된 형사소송법을 안 읽어봐서 그런데, 개정된 형소법에 의하면 검사는 수사하면 안 된다고 되어 있느냐”고 했다. 불과 24시간 전 국민 다수의 반대를 무릅쓰고 국무회의에서 의결한 법안을 대통령이 읽어보지도 않았다는 게 말이 되는가. 게다가 이 대통령은 거부권을 행사하지 않은 이유까지 상세히 밝히지 않았나. 그렇다면 “입법권을 부정할 만큼 심각한 상황이라고 보기는 어렵다”거나 “사필귀정의 필연적 조치”라는 판단은 법안을 읽지도 않고 한 게 된다. 이재명 대통령과 정성호 법무부 장관이 4일 청와대에서 열린 국무회의에서 국민의례를 하고 있다. [청와대사진기자단] 무책임한 발언이라는 지적이 나오자 청와대는 “대통령께서는 형소법 개정의 핵심 내용을 당연히 숙지하고 계신다”고 수습했고, 여권에선 법 개정을 주도한 여당 강경파와 생각이 다르다는 점을 표출한 것이라는 해석이 나왔다. 법안을 숙지하고 문제점을 알면서도 거부권을 안 썼다면 안 읽은 것보다 더 큰 직무유기가 아닌가. 논란을 의식한 듯 이 대통령은 어제 수석보좌관회의에서는 “항상 국민의 눈높이에서 모든 사안을 살피고 문제가 있으면 어떤 사항도 성역 없이 적극적으로 고치는 유연하고 능동적인 행정이 필요하다”고 했다. 대통령의 소신과 발언, 그리고 실제 정책 집행이 다르게 돌아가니 국민만 혼란스러울 뿐이다. 논란을 야기한 검경 합동수사본부 운영에 대한 대통령의 질문에 주무 부처 장관들의 답변이 엇갈린 것도 국민 눈높이에선 어처구니없는 노릇이다. 정성호 법무부 장관은 “검사가 합동 수사할 수 있는 근거는 없다”고 했고, 윤호중 행안부 장관은 “검사가 수사에 관해 의견은 낼 수 있다”고 했다. 70년 넘게 운영된 형사사법 체계를 뒤흔드는 법안이 국회와 국무회의를 통과하는 동안 주무장관들이 가장 기초적인 사안에 대한 입장을 정리하지 못했다는 건 심각한 국정 공백 상황이다. 다수의 국민과 범죄 피해자들까지 뻔히 내다보며 걱정한 사안을 주무장관들은 논의 한 번 안 한 것이기 때문이다. 백번 양보하더라도 이틀 전 국무회의 심의에서는 이견을 정리했어야 할 것 아닌가. 그러니 형소법 개정이 마지막 순간까지 졸속으로 이뤄졌다는 말이 나오는 것이다.

editorial.titleTr: Opinion: President Who Didn't Read Criminal Procedure Act Leaves Cabinet Ministers with Conflicting Interpretations
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung rejected the criminal procedure law amendment without reading it.
The presidential office attempted damage control by claiming it was aware of the matter, but relevant ministers gave conflicting answers.
A major overhaul of the criminal justice system after 70 years is being rushed through amid a policy vacuum.
editorial.bodyTr: At a Cabinet meeting presided over by President Lee Jae-myung two days ago, remarks that left the public bewildered came pouring out. The president asked, "I haven't read the revised Criminal Procedure Act, but according to the revised law, does it say that prosecutors cannot conduct investigations?" How can it be explained that the president had not even read a bill that was approved at a Cabinet meeting just 24 hours earlier, despite opposition from the majority of the public? Moreover, did the president not provide detailed reasons for not exercising his veto power? If so, then judgments such as "it is difficult to view this as a situation grave enough to deny legislative authority" or "a necessary measure of inevitability" were made without reading the bill. When criticism emerged that this was an irresponsible remark, the Blue House responded that "the president naturally understands the core contents of the criminal procedure law amendments," and the ruling bloc offered an interpretation that the president was expressing a different view from the hardline faction of the ruling party that led the law's revision. If the president was aware of the bill and understood its problems yet failed to exercise his veto, is that not a greater dereliction of duty than not reading it at all? As if conscious of the controversy, the president said at a senior aides meeting yesterday, "flexible and proactive administration that always views all matters from the perspective of the people's expectations and actively corrects any problems without exception is necessary." Since the president's convictions, statements, and actual policy implementation diverge, only the public becomes confused. It is equally absurd from the people's perspective that cabinet ministers gave conflicting responses to the president's question regarding the operation of the joint investigation unit between prosecutors and police that sparked the controversy. Justice Minister Jung Sung-ho said "there is no basis for prosecutors to conduct joint investigations," while Interior Minister Yoon Ho-jung said "prosecutors can offer opinions on investigations." The fact that during the passage of a bill that shakes the criminal justice system operated for over 70 years through the National Assembly and Cabinet meeting, the responsible ministers failed to clarify their positions on the most fundamental issues represents a serious vacuum in state governance. The responsible ministers did not even have a single discussion on the matters that many citizens and crime victims openly worried about. Even if we make a hundred concessions, should the differences not have been resolved during the Cabinet meeting two days ago? This is why there is talk that the criminal procedure law amendment was rushed through to the very last moment.

leanScore.label: Lean progressive
leanScore.rationale: 검찰 수사권 제한 개정안을 지지하면서 대통령과 정부의 무능과 졸속 입법을 비판하는 진보 성향의 법치주의 입장

editorials.title: [사설] 증시 폭락 겪고도 “경제 견실” 딴소리하는 정부
editorials.body: 입력 업데이트 종합 26면 정부가 한국 증시의 극심한 변동성과 정책 혼선을 지적한 외신 보도에 잇따라 해명과 반박을 내놓고 있다. 하지만 정책 실패에 대한 비판에 경제 펀더멘털을 강조하는 식으로 초점에서 비켜난 대응을 하고 있다는 게 문제다. 구윤철 부총리 겸 재정경제부 장관이 지난달 31일 서울 종로구 정부서울청사에서 열린 비상경제본부회의 겸 경제관계장관회의 겸 민생물가 특별관리 관계장관 TF에서 모두발언을 하고 있다. 뉴스1 앞서 미국 경제매체 블룸버그는 ‘한국이 투자부적합(uninvestable) 국가가 되고 있다’는 내용의 칼럼을 게재했다. 칼럼은 한국 증시가 단 27거래일 만에 40% 급락하는 등 극심한 변동성을 보이며 투자 심리가 크게 훼손되고 있다고 지적했다. 그러면서 변동성을 키운 주요 원인으로 단일종목 레버리지 상장지수펀드(ETF) 도입과 국민연금의 석연치 않은 국내 투자 비중 확대 등 정책 혼선을 꼽았다. 이에 대해 구윤철 경제부총리는 어제 “한국 경제는 그 어느 때보다 견실하고, 전례 없는 성과를 시현 중”이라며 “증시 변동성 완화를 위해 신속하게 대응하고 있으며, 최근에는 주가지수도 안정화하는 흐름을 보이고 있다”고 밝혔다. 앞서 금융위원회가 한국 경제의 ‘견조한 펀더멘털’을 강조하며 “투자 부적격 국가로 평가될 우려는 전혀 없다”고 공식 반박한 것과 같은 맥락이다. 구 부총리의 반박을 들은 많은 투자자는 어이없었을 것이다. 어제도 코스피 시장에선 삼성전자(-6.3%)와 SK하이닉스(-10.37%)가 급락하며 어김없이 매도 사이드카가 발동됐다. 올해 들어서만 벌써 46번째 사이드카다. 이게 부총리가 주장하는 주가지수 안정화의 모습인가. 금융시장이 망가지는데도 펀더멘털을 강조하는 부총리의 모습은 30년 전 외환위기가 덮칠 당시 한국 경제에 문제가 없다고 했던 IMF의 펀더멘털론이 떠오르게 할 정도다. 정작 김용범 청와대 정책실장을 필두로 한 경제팀은 위험성이 큰 상품을 도입하면서도 사전에 취약성을 점검하는 절차(스트레스 테스트)를 거치지 않았다는 의혹을 받고 있다. 명확한 진상 규명과 책임자 문책을 요구하는 목소리가 커지고 있지만, 청와대 홍보소통수석은 어제 “지금은 대책을 챙기는 것이 중요한 사항”이라며 답을 비켜나갔다. 그러나 이런 책임 회피성 대응은 정부 정책 역량에 대한 불신만 키울 뿐이다. 대형 화재로 큰 피해를 보았건만 불이 난 이유를 내놓지 않고 있는 형국이기 때문이다.

editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Government Claims Economy Is Sound Despite Stock Market Plunge
summaryTr: Despite the stock market plunge, the government shirks responsibility by only emphasizing economic fundamentals
Policy confusion, including the introduction of single-stock ETFs, is a major driver of heightened volatility
Need to clarify economic team's accountability for introducing risky products without prior verification procedures
editorials.bodyTr:
The government has been issuing repeated clarifications and rebuttals in response to foreign media reports pointing out extreme volatility in the Korean stock market and policy confusion. However, the problem is that it is responding to criticism of policy failures by shifting focus, emphasizing economic fundamentals instead. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance Koo Yoon-chul made opening remarks at an emergency economic meeting held at the Government Seoul Building in Jongno-gu, Seoul, on the 31st of last month, along with an economic ministers' meeting and a special task force meeting on people's livelihoods and prices. News1.

Previously, American economic media outlet Bloomberg published a column stating that "Korea is becoming an uninvestable country." The column pointed out that the Korean stock market is experiencing extreme volatility, with a 40 percent plunge in just 27 trading days, causing significant damage to investment sentiment. It cited policy confusion as a major factor driving this volatility, including the introduction of single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds and the National Pension Service's questionable expansion of domestic investment allocation. In response, Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yoon-chul said yesterday, "The Korean economy is sound as never before and is demonstrating unprecedented achievements," adding that "we are responding swiftly to ease stock market volatility, and recently stock indices are showing signs of stabilization." This mirrors the Financial Services Commission's earlier official rebuttal, in which it emphasized the Korean economy's "solid fundamentals" and stated there was "no concern whatsoever" about the country being rated as an unsuitable investment destination.

Many investors who heard Deputy Prime Minister Koo's rebuttal must have been incredulous. Yesterday as well, Samsung Electronics fell 6.3 percent and SK Hynix dropped 10.37 percent on the KOSPI market, triggering the sell-side circuit breaker without fail. That was the 46th circuit breaker of the year alone. Is this what the deputy prime minister claims is stock index stabilization? The sight of the deputy prime minister emphasizing fundamentals while the financial market crumbles brings to mind the IMF's fundamentals theory from 30 years ago, when it said there were no problems with the Korean economy as the foreign exchange crisis loomed. In fact, the economic team led by Blue House Policy Director Kim Yong-beom is facing suspicions that it introduced high-risk products without undergoing prior procedures to examine vulnerabilities, namely stress tests. Voices calling for clear clarification of facts and accountability are growing louder, but the Blue House spokesman for publicity and communication dodged the question yesterday, saying "what is important now is to address countermeasures." However, this evasive response only breeds distrust in the government's policy capacity. It is like having suffered major damage from a large fire but not revealing why the fire started.

editorials.title: [사설] 지방대 살리기 해법이 왜 하필 등록금 면제인가
editorials.body: 입력 종합 26면 최교진 교육부 장관이 2025년 112월 12일 정부세종컨벤션센터에서 이재명 대통령에게 업무보고를 하고 있다. 왼쪽부터 최은옥 교육부 차관, 최 장관, 차정인 국가교육위원장. [연합뉴스] 교육부가 30개 지방 국립대(9개 지방 거점 국립대와 일반 국립대) 학생들에게 ‘지역 균형 장학금’을 지급하는 방안을 검토하고 있다고 지난 5일 대통령 업무보고에서 밝혔다. 이르면 내년에 신입생에게 등록금 전액을 지급하고, 예산 확보 규모에 따라 다른 학년으로 확대할 방침이다. 내년부터 모든 신입생의 등록금을 면제해 주려면 약 1000억원의 추가 예산이 필요하고, 1~4학년 전체로 수혜 대상을 넓히면 연간 4000억원의 예산을 더 투입해야 한다. 우선 정책 실효성에 의문이 든다. 등록금을 면제해 주면 학생들이 몰린 것이란 진단부터가 현실적이지 않다. 현재 30개 지방 국립대 학생 중 60%가 국가장학금을 받고 있는데도 우수한 수험생들은 등록금을 감수하고 수도권으로 몰리는 게 현실이다. 우수한 교수진 초빙이나 교육의 질 향상과 혁신을 위한 투자, 취업·창업 등 일자리와 연계된 프로그램 개발 등에 재원을 투입하는 게 효과는 더딜지 모르지만 더 중요하고 본질적인 해법일 것이다. 교육부의 정책 방침이 알려지면서 형평성 논란도 제기되고 있다. 지방 국립대에 혜택이 집중되면 가뜩이나 학생 충원이 어려워 재정 사정이 더 열악한 지방 사립대의 역차별 문제가 생긴다. 수도권 사립대도 어렵기는 마찬가지다. 교육부가 2009년부터 국가장학금 카드를 무기 삼아 사립대 등록금을 사실상 반강제로 동결해 대학 재정 상황을 왜곡해 왔다. 이 때문에 대학생 1인당 공교육비가 지방교육재정교부금(내국세의 20.97% 배정)이 대거 투입되는 초등학생보다 적은 교육재정 왜곡 현상이 초래됐다. 취업에 유리하다는 생각으로 수도권 사립대에 진학한 지방 출신 학생 역시 장학금 차별을 받게 된다. 지역 인재가 수도권으로 유출되는 것을 예방하고 대학 진학 단계부터 지방에 정착하도록 유도하고, 나아가 교육을 통해 지역 균형 발전의 토대를 쌓겠다는 방향에는 공감할 수 있다. 하지만 그 방법으로 등록금 면제가 우선인지는 의문이다. 교육 당국은 등록금 면제와 같은 현금 나눠주기성 정책보다는 보다 더 근본적인 교육 개혁 방안을 내놓아야 할 것이다.

등록금 면제만으로는 우수 학생의 수도권 유출을 막기 어렵다는 지적이다.

editorials.titleTr: Why Is Tuition Waiver the Answer to Saving Regional Universities?
summaryTr: The Ministry of Education is pushing ahead with a plan to fully waive tuition for incoming students at regional national universities.
Experts point out that tuition waivers alone will struggle to prevent top students from leaving for the Seoul metropolitan area.
They argue that fundamental reforms such as recruiting distinguished professors and innovating education are more critical solutions.
editorials.bodyTr: The Ministry of Education announced in a presidential briefing on the 5th that it is reviewing plans to provide "regional balance scholarships" to students at 30 local national universities, comprising nine regional hub national universities and general national universities. The plan is to cover full tuition for new students as early as next year, with expansion to other grade levels depending on budget availability. Providing tuition exemptions for all new students starting next year would require approximately 100 billion won in additional budget, while extending benefits to all students in grades one through four would require an additional 400 billion won annually. First, there are doubts about the policy's actual effectiveness. The diagnosis that providing tuition exemptions would draw students is not realistic. Currently, 60 percent of students at the 30 local national universities receive national scholarships, yet in reality, top-performing students bear the tuition burden and still migrate to Seoul and surrounding areas. Rather than tuition exemptions, directing resources toward recruiting outstanding faculty, investing in educational quality improvement and innovation, and developing job-linked programs in employment and entrepreneurship may have delayed effects but would represent a more important and fundamental solution. Fairness concerns have also been raised as the Ministry of Education's policy direction becomes known. If benefits become concentrated at local national universities, the already severe student recruitment difficulties at local private universities could create reverse discrimination problems due to their already strained financial situations. Seoul metropolitan private universities face similar difficulties. Since 2009, the Ministry of Education has wielded national scholarship cards as a weapon to effectively freeze private university tuition by force, distorting university finances. This has resulted in per-capita public education spending for university students being lower than that for elementary school students, who receive substantial allocations from local education finance transfer funds, which account for 20.97 percent of domestic tax revenue. Provincial students who enrolled at Seoul metropolitan private universities under the belief they would have better employment prospects also face scholarship discrimination. The goal of preventing talented regional youth from flowing to Seoul, encouraging settlement in local areas from the university entrance stage onward, and ultimately laying the foundation for regional balanced development through education is understandable. However, whether tuition exemptions should be the priority method is questionable. Education authorities must present more fundamental educational reform measures rather than cash distribution policies such as tuition exemptions.

editorial.title: Leveraged ETF fallout
editorial.body: Korea must restore policy credibility after financial populism fuels market turmoil Markets have a habit of exposing political wishful thinking. They can absorb disappointing earnings and slower growth. They are far less forgiving when governments try to rewrite the rules by which prices are set. South Korea's recent stock market turmoil offers a costly reminder. The catalyst was single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. They debuted in late May as enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence and semiconductor shares approached its peak. Instead of merely amplifying investor interest, the products intensified every subsequent decline. Violent swings through June and July triggered automatic liquidations, repeated trading halts and heavy losses for retail investors. Regulators later tightened investment requirements and suspended additional launches, sharply reducing trading activity. Those emergency steps calmed speculation, yet they arrived only after the damage had spread. Many have portrayed the turmoil as another chapter in the global technology correction or the semiconductor cycle. Those forces clearly mattered. But they do not explain why Korea’s benchmark index became one of the world's most turbulent major equity markets within weeks. The answer lies partly in market structure. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix already dominate the benchmark index. Introducing derivatives that doubled daily price movements concentrated even greater pressure on an already narrow market. Daily portfolio rebalancing and margin requirements then reinforced each decline. Falling prices prompted forced selling, which drove prices lower and generated fresh liquidations, creating a feedback loop that spread well beyond the semiconductor sector. What began as a correction in a handful of stocks distorted price formation across the broader market. This turned an ordinary downturn into a painful breakdown in market stability. The authorities' response inadvertently made the point. They accelerated plans to raise the minimum cash deposit from 10 million won ($7,050) to 30 million won, examined portfolio exposure limits and halted new listings of similar products. Those measures were sensible. They also suggested that safeguards deserved closer scrutiny before the products ever reached investors. Equally troubling is the speed with which such a consequential policy reached the market. Opposition parties have demanded investigations, while criticism has spread beyond partisan lines. Even figures broadly aligned with the Lee Jae Myung administration have called for a closer examination of the approval process for the leveraged ETFs. The issue extends beyond one financial product. Transparent decision-making is essential because trust in financial supervision depends as much on institutional independence as regulatory expertise. When policy initiatives appear to originate in political offices while regulators adjust course afterward, the boundary between oversight and political direction inevitably becomes blurred. Foreign media’s portrayal of Korea as an unpredictable investment destination may overstate the case, and government officials are right to point to robust exports, healthy corporate earnings and solid macroeconomic indicators. Yet sound fundamentals cannot fully offset doubts created when financial rules appear vulnerable to shifting political priorities rather than consistent regulatory judgment. That distinction matters because the “Korea discount” has never reflected corporate performance alone. Investors evaluate the credibility of policymaking. Sudden regulatory shifts, emergency interventions and uncertainty over who ultimately directs financial oversight inevitably raise the premium global investors demand. A transparent review of how single-stock leveraged ETFs won approval would therefore strengthen the market rather than weaken it. It should clarify whether internal objections received adequate consideration and whether institutional safeguards functioned as intended. Speculative enthusiasm can lift share prices for a time, but lasting gains depend on institutional credibility. The government is moving to stabilize markets and rebuild confidence. Assuming belated measures can quickly restore trust would itself be another form of political wishful thinking. summaryTr: 한국의 레버리지 ETF 위기는 상품이 반도체 주가 변동을 증폭시키면서 결함 있는 시장 구조를 드러냈다.
강제 청산과 자동 거래 중단이 광범위한 시장 전역으로 확산되면서 기술주 부문을 넘어 가격을 불안정하게 했다.
규제 당국의 늦은 긴급 조치와 불명확한 승인 절차는 금융 감시에 대한 투자자 신뢰를 위협하고 있다.
editorial.bodyTr:
금융 포퓰리즘이 시장 혼란을 초래한 후 한국은 정책 신뢰성을 회복해야 한다

시장은 정치적 희망사항을 드러내는 습성이 있다. 실망스러운 실적과 성장 둔화는 흡수할 수 있다. 가격이 결정되는 규칙을 정부가 다시 쓰려고 할 때는 훨씬 덜 관대하다. 한국의 최근 주식시장 혼란은 비용이 많이 드는 경고를 제공한다. 촉발 요인은 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스에 연동된 단일 종목 레버리지 상장지수펀드(ETF)였다. 인공지능과 반도체 주식을 둘러싼 열정이 정점에 가까워질 무렵 5월 말에 출시되었다. 단순히 투자자 관심을 증폭시키는 대신 이 상품들은 그 이후의 모든 하락을 심화시켰다. 6월과 7월을 거치면서 폭력적인 변동은 자동 청산, 반복적인 거래 중단, 개인투자자들의 큰 손실을 초래했다. 규제 당국은 나중에 투자 요건을 강화하고 추가 출시를 중단했으며, 거래량을 급격히 감소시켰다. 이러한 긴급 조치들은 투기를 진정시켰지만, 피해가 확산된 이후에야 도입되었다. 많은 사람들이 이러한 혼란을 글로벌 기술 조정이나 반도체 사이클의 또 다른 장으로 묘사했다. 이러한 요인들이 분명히 중요했다. 하지만 한국의 벤치마크 지수가 수주 내에 세계에서 가장 변동성 높은 주요 주식시장 중 하나가 된 이유를 설명하지는 못한다. 답은 부분적으로 시장 구조에 있다. 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스는 이미 벤치마크 지수를 지배하고 있다. 일일 가격 변동을 두 배로 늘리는 파생상품을 도입하면 이미 좁은 시장에 더욱 큰 압력을 집중시켰다. 일일 포트폴리오 리밸런싱과 증거금 요건이 각 하락을 강화했다. 가격 하락이 강제 매도를 초래했고, 이는 가격을 더 낮추고 새로운 청산을 만들어내며 반도체 부문을 훨씬 넘어 확산되는 악순환을 만들었다. 소수 종목의 조정으로 시작된 것이 광범위한 시장 전반의 가격 형성을 왜곡했다. 이는 일상적인 하락을 시장 안정성의 고통스러운 붕괴로 변모시켰다.

당국의 대응은 뜻하지 않게 이를 입증했다. 최소 현금 예치금을 1천만 원에서 3천만 원으로 인상할 계획을 가속화하고, 포트폴리오 노출 한도를 검토하며, 유사 상품의 신규 상장을 중단했다. 이러한 조치들은 합리적이었다. 또한 상품이 투자자에게 닿기 전에 보호장치를 더 철저히 검토할 필요가 있음을 시사했다. 마찬가지로 문제인 것은 이렇게 중대한 정책이 시장에 도달한 속도이다. 야당은 조사를 요구했으며, 비판은 진영을 초월해 확산되었다. 이재명 행정부와 광범위하게 일치하는 인물들조차 레버리지 ETF 승인 과정을 더 면밀히 검토할 것을 촉구했다.

문제는 하나의 금융상품을 벗어난다. 투명한 의사결정은 필수적이다. 금융감시에 대한 신뢰는 규제 전문성만큼 제도적 독립성에 달려 있기 때문이다. 정책 주도권이 정치 사무소에서 나온 것처럼 보이고 규제 당국이 이후에 방침을 조정할 때, 감시와 정치적 방향 사이의 경계는 필연적으로 흐려진다. 외신이 한국을 예측 불가능한 투자 대상으로 묘사한 것은 과장일 수 있으며, 정부 관리들이 강건한 수출, 건강한 기업 수익, 견고한 거시경제 지표를 지적하는 것은 맞다. 하지만 금융 규칙이 일관된 규제 판단보다 변화하는 정치적 우선순위에 취약해 보일 때 창출되는 의구심을 건전한 기초만으로는 완전히 상쇄할 수 없다. 이러한 구분은 중요하다. editorials.title: Leveraged ETF fallout
editorials.body: Korea must restore policy credibility after financial populism fuels market turmoil Markets have a habit of exposing political wishful thinking. They can absorb disappointing earnings and slower growth. They are far less forgiving when governments try to rewrite the rules by which prices are set. South Korea's recent stock market turmoil offers a costly reminder. The catalyst was single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. They debuted in late May as enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence and semiconductor shares approached its peak. Instead of merely amplifying investor interest, the products intensified every subsequent decline. Violent swings through June and July triggered automatic liquidations, repeated trading halts and heavy losses for retail investors. Regulators later tightened investment requirements and suspended additional launches, sharply reducing trading activity. Those emergency steps calmed speculation, yet they arrived only after the damage had spread. Many have portrayed the turmoil as another chapter in the global technology correction or the semiconductor cycle. Those forces clearly mattered. But they do not explain why Korea’s benchmark index became one of the world's most turbulent major equity markets within weeks. The answer lies partly in market structure. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix already dominate the benchmark index. Introducing derivatives that doubled daily price movements concentrated even greater pressure on an already narrow market. Daily portfolio rebalancing and margin requirements then reinforced each decline. Falling prices prompted forced selling, which drove prices lower and generated fresh liquidations, creating a feedback loop that spread well beyond the semiconductor sector. What began as a correction in a handful of stocks distorted price formation across the broader market. This turned an ordinary downturn into a painful breakdown in market stability. The authorities' response inadvertently made the point. They accelerated plans to raise the minimum cash deposit from 10 million won ($7,050) to 30 million won, examined portfolio exposure limits and halted new listings of similar products. Those measures were sensible. They also suggested that safeguards deserved closer scrutiny before the products ever reached investors. Equally troubling is the speed with which such a consequential policy reached the market. Opposition parties have demanded investigations, while criticism has spread beyond partisan lines. Even figures broadly aligned with the Lee Jae Myung administration have called for a closer examination of the approval process for the leveraged ETFs. The issue extends beyond one financial product. Transparent decision-making is essential because trust in financial supervision depends as much on institutional independence as regulatory expertise. When policy initiatives appear to originate in political offices while regulators adjust course afterward, the boundary between oversight and political direction inevitably becomes blurred. Foreign media’s portrayal of Korea as an unpredictable investment destination may overstate the case, and government officials are right to point to robust exports, healthy corporate earnings and solid macroeconomic indicators. Yet sound fundamentals cannot fully offset doubts created when financial rules appear vulnerable to shifting political priorities rather than consistent regulatory judgment. That distinction matters because the “Korea discount” has never reflected corporate performance alone. Investors evaluate the credibility of policymaking. Sudden regulatory shifts, emergency interventions and uncertainty over who ultimately directs financial oversight inevitably raise the premium global investors demand. A transparent review of how single-stock leveraged ETFs won approval would therefore strengthen the market rather than weaken it. It should clarify whether internal objections received adequate consideration and whether institutional safeguards functioned as intended. Speculative enthusiasm can lift share prices for a time, but lasting gains depend on institutional credibility. The government is moving to stabilize markets and rebuild confidence. Assuming belated measures can quickly restore trust would itself be another form of political wishful thinking. editorial.bodyTr: The U.S. Department of Defense is reportedly discussing a new nuclear strategy that emphasizes the use of short-range tactical nuclear weapons to defend allied nations in the event of localized conflicts with China and Russia.
